label: Editorial. Hand-written for this app, not copied from anywhere. The title and race numbers come from the data tabs; the rest is a fan's summary, so check anything important against official sources.

eras.title: The founding years
eras.text: The world championship started in 1950 with pre-war machines, huge front engines and drivers who raced in cloth caps. Alfa Romeo ruled the first seasons, then Ferrari and Mercedes took over. Juan Manuel Fangio won five titles with four different teams. Near the end of the decade a small British team, Cooper, put the engine behind the driver and quietly changed the sport.

eras.title: Garagistes and rear engines
eras.text: Rear-engined cars won everything, and small British builders such as Lotus, Brabham and BRM beat the big names. Jim Clark became the template for a driver who made hard things look easy. The sport was also deadly. Drivers took the risk as normal, and the push for safety only began late in the decade.

eras.title: Wings, sponsors and survival
eras.text: Wings and later ground effect showed that air could matter as much as the engine. Cigarette and other sponsor colours covered the cars, and Bernie Ecclestone began turning team rights into a business. In 1976 Niki Lauda came back to racing weeks after a near-fatal crash and lost the title to James Hunt by a single point.

eras.title: Turbos and rivals
eras.text: Turbo engines pushed power past 1000 hp in qualifying trim. The decade belongs to Alain Prost and Ayrton Senna, team-mates at McLaren and then enemies. Their fights over the 1989 and 1990 titles are still argued about. McLaren in 1988 was about as dominant as a team gets.

eras.title: Electronics and loss
eras.text: Computers took over the cars: active suspension, traction control, semi-automatic gearboxes. In 1994 Ayrton Senna and Roland Ratzenberger died at Imola in the same weekend. Safety rules and circuit changes followed, and the next driver death from a race crash came more than twenty years later. Michael Schumacher arrived in 1991 and began a run that would define the next era.

eras.title: The red years and the reset
eras.text: Schumacher and Ferrari took five straight titles from 2000 to 2004. Fernando Alonso and Renault ended it in 2005 and 2006. Hybrid ideas, tyre wars and refuelling came and went. In 2009 a new rule set let Brawn GP, a team built from the ashes of Honda, win the title in its only season.

eras.title: Vettel, then the hybrid age
eras.text: Sebastian Vettel and Red Bull won four titles in a row from 2010. From 2014, quiet and complex hybrid power units arrived and Mercedes got them right. Lewis Hamilton and Nico Rosberg fought as team-mates, then Hamilton ran away with the sport and had six titles by 2019.

eras.title: Cost caps and ground effect
eras.text: A pandemic season opened the decade. Budget caps arrived, and ground-effect cars returned in 2022. Max Verstappen and Hamilton fought the 2021 title down to the last lap of the last race. Verstappen then dominated, until McLarens caught up and Lando Norris won the 2025 title.

moments.title: Silverstone, round one
moments.text: The first world championship race, 13 May at Silverstone. Nino Farina went on to win the first drivers' title that year (see History tab).

moments.title: Lauda's return
moments.text: Niki Lauda crashed badly at the Nurburgring, then raced again about six weeks later. Hunt took the title by one point.

moments.title: Senna's first title
moments.text: Ayrton Senna beat team-mate Alain Prost for the 1988 drivers' title with McLaren. The History tab shows his points.

moments.title: Imola
moments.text: A black weekend that changed safety in motorsport for good.

moments.title: The end of the Schumacher run
moments.text: Alonso became the youngest champion at that time and ended Ferrari's five-year run (see History tab).

moments.title: Hamilton's first title
moments.text: Lewis Hamilton won his first title on the final lap of the final race in Brazil, by a single point over Felipe Massa.

moments.title: Brawn GP
moments.text: A team that nearly folded won both titles in its only year of existence.

moments.title: Abu Dhabi
moments.text: Verstappen and Hamilton arrived at the last race level on points. The title was decided on the last lap.

moments.title: Norris takes it
moments.text: Lando Norris won the 2025 drivers' championship, McLaren's first drivers' title since 2008 (see History tab for the numbers).
